title: Then-and-now table
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: Ocean exploration in the 19th century (Blue Abyss)
source: Seeded from history/y4 lesson 20 (Then-and-now table (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 20: Exploring the ocean then and now. To understand how ocean exploration has changed since the Challenger expedition

questions.q: Which is faster: rope sounding or sonar?
questions.model: A rope has to be lowered by hand. Sound travels to the bottom and back in seconds. So sonar is faster.

questions.q: Name one thing that has stayed the same.
Who wrote sailing guides to the Indian Ocean in the 1400s?
Complete a then-and-now table (depth, samples, travel, light) and write one change and one continuity sentence.
questions.a: Accurate table and two sentences, e.g. depth by rope then, sonar now
questions.model: Teacher fills the depth row first.

questions.q: Which modern tool would have helped Challenger most? Why?
questions.a: For example: sonar, because one depth would take seconds, not hours

questions.q: Why do we still not know everything about the deep ocean?
questions.a: It is huge, dark and under great pressure, so it is hard and costly to reach

questions.q: Big question: easier or harder today?
questions.a: Easier and faster with sonar and robots, but the deep is still hard to reach
